name: Example: Finding the Real or Imaginary Part of a Scalar Given the Conjugate of a Scaled Vector
worked_solution:
Since $\overline{k\mathbf{v}} = \overline{k} \, \overline{\mathbf{v}},$ we get the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{kv} & =\overset{―}{k}\,\overset{―}{v} \\ [\begin{aligned}8\text{i}-12 \\ 0\end{aligned}] & =\overset{―}{k}\,\overset{―}{[\begin{aligned}-4\text{i} \\ 0\end{aligned}]} \\ [\begin{aligned}8\text{i}-12 \\ 0\end{aligned}] & =\overset{―}{k}\,[\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{-4\text{i}} \\ \overset{―}{0}\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}8\text{i}-12 \\ 0\end{aligned}] & =\overset{―}{k}\,[\begin{aligned}4\text{i} \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}8\text{i}-12 \\ 0\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}4\text{i}\,\overset{―}{k} \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, we obtain that 

$$
4\textrm{i}\,\overline{k}  = 8\textrm{i}-12
\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
\overline{k}=\dfrac{8\textrm{i}-12}{4\textrm i} = 2+3\textrm{i}.
$$

 

Therefore, $k=\overline{2+3\textrm{i}}=2-3\textrm{i}.$

Finally, $\textrm{Im}(k)=-3.$
